fact: Older adults (>60y) require ≥2.8g leucine (~30g protein) per meal to stimulate MPS. Younger adults (<30y) show near-linear MPS response to protein content with no strict leucine threshold.
practical_application: At 28y, total per-meal protein (30-40g) is sufficient. No need to obsess over leucine thresholds.

fact: Post-meal MPS anabolic response lasts 2-3 hours. Single large protein dinner is suboptimal. 4-5 meals spaced 3-4h apart maximizes total daily MPS.
practical_application: 4-5 meals of 35-45g protein each, spaced 3-4h apart.

fact: Total daily protein intake is the most important dietary factor for lean body mass. At ≥1.6 g/kg/day, distribution and quality matter less.
practical_application: Hit ≥160g/day consistently first, then optimize distribution.

fact: Dose-dependent association between dietary leucine and post-exercise MPS. Relationship plateaus at higher doses.
practical_application: Ensure 2-3g leucine per major meal (~30-40g quality protein).

fact: Plant-based diets can supply enough protein and leucine to maximize hypertrophy if ~2g leucine/meal threshold is met through combining.
practical_application: Soya chunks + paneer + Greek yogurt for vegetarian days.

fact: Balanced protein distribution (4-5 evenly spaced feedings of 30-40g) maximizes post-prandial MPS vs skewed distribution.
sources: Lak et al., Frontiers in Nutrition, 2024
practical_application: Breakfast 40g, Lunch 40g, Snack 30g, Dinner 50g, Pre-bed 30g = ~190g.

fact: Protein quality matters less at higher total intakes (≥1.6g/kg/day). Vegan and omnivorous high-protein diets produce comparable myofibrillar protein synthesis.
sources: Layman DK, 2024; Monteyne et al., J Nutrition, 2023
practical_application: Vary protein sources across the day; don't stress about combining at every meal.

fact: The 30-minute 'anabolic window' is a myth. Meta-analysis shows protein timing around exercise does not influence adaptations when total daily protein is matched.
practical_application: Don't stress about immediate post-workout shakes. Hit daily protein.

fact: 8-week RCT: protein immediately before/after vs 3h before/after = no significant difference in gains. Both groups improved equally.
sources: Lak et al., Frontiers in Nutrition, 2024
practical_application: Train and eat when convenient.

fact: Prior meta-analyses suggesting timing matters were limited by inactive comparator designs (control got no protein at all).
sources: Lak et al., 2024; Schoenfeld et al., 2013
practical_application: Supplement industry timing claims are based on flawed studies.

fact: Anabolic window is wider (~4-6h) than thought. Modest benefit to protein within hours post-training, especially if fasted or pre-workout meal was >4h prior.
sources: Deane et al., Frontiers in Nutrition, 2024
practical_application: If training fasted, eat within 1-2h post-workout.

fact: Daily protein threshold for maximizing hypertrophy: ~1.62 g/kg bodyweight/day. Beyond this, diminishing returns.
practical_application: Target 1.6g/kg of lean/ideal mass = ~180-200g for Achyut.

fact: No direct meta-analysis evidence that carb cycling is superior to consistent caloric intake for body recomposition. Supported by tradition, not RCTs.
practical_application: For beginners, consistent moderate deficit is simpler and equally effective.

fact: High-carb diets better maintain exercise performance vs low-carb, but body composition changes are similar when protein/calories matched.
practical_application: Keep carbs moderate-to-high on training days for performance.

fact: Multi-component programs (IF + carb cycling + exercise) improve body composition, but unclear which component drives results.
practical_application: Overall approach works; carb cycling specifically may not add value.

fact: Key factors for lean mass sparing during caloric restriction: protein ≥1.6g/kg, resistance training volume, moderate deficit. Carb manipulation is secondary.
practical_application: Focus on protein + training + moderate deficit, not carb timing.

fact: True recomposition (simultaneous fat loss + lean gain) is achievable in beginners and overweight individuals. Carb cycling not required.
practical_application: As 130 kg beginner, recomposition is very achievable with fundamentals.

fact: Sodium sweat loss: 500-2000mg/hour depending on intensity and heat. At 1L/hour sweat rate, ~2% total body sodium lost per hour.
practical_application: 300-500mg sodium pre-workout for sessions >60 min.

fact: Pre-workout sodium loading (500-1000mg in 500-750ml water, 60-90 min pre) enhances plasma volume and pump.
sources: Blow et al., 2025; ISSN position stands
practical_application: 1/4 tsp salt in 500ml water before training, especially in Ghaziabad heat.

fact: Exercise-associated muscle cramping is primarily from muscle fatigue/neuromuscular issues, NOT dehydration/electrolyte imbalance (though sodium can contribute in prolonged heat exercise).
practical_application: Address cramping with warm-up and technique, not just salt.

fact: Co-transport of water + sodium enhances hydration more than plain water during exercise.
practical_application: Add salt + glucose to water for long sessions (ORS principle).

fact: ISSN recommends 300-600mg sodium/hour for exercise >1 hour. For <60 min sessions, normal dietary sodium is sufficient.
practical_application: Pre-workout salt optional for 45-60 min lifting. Indian food is well-salted.

fact: Meta-analysis: fasted vs fed resistance training produces similar gains in fat-free mass, hypertrophy, and strength when total daily nutrition matched.
sources: Vieira et al., J Bodywork Mov Ther, 2025
practical_application: Fasted training is fine if mornings work best.

fact: RCT: fasted vs fed resistance training = similar hypertrophy and strength gains. Fasted did NOT impair muscle growth.
practical_application: Train when consistent. Eat protein-rich meal after.

fact: Ramadan fasting study: both fasted and fed groups maintained strength and hypertrophy.
practical_application: Training during fasting is safe and effective.

fact: Exercise enhances anabolic sensitivity to protein feeding for up to 24h. Fasted training has modest advantage to fed state for acute MPS.
practical_application: If training fasted, eat high-protein meal within 1-2h post-workout.

fact: Both acute and chronic alcohol decrease MPS and increase protein degradation via mTORC1 pathway inhibition.
sources: Simon et al., Alcohol Research: Current Reviews, 2023
practical_application: Minimize or eliminate alcohol during serious training phases.

fact: Single binge (BAC ≥0.08, ~4-5 drinks) can cause acute myopathy and impairs MPS for 24h+.
practical_application: Binge drinking post-workout is worst-case for muscle growth.

fact: 40-60% of chronic heavy drinkers develop alcohol-related myopathy. Chronic use increases breakdown via UPP/atrogenes.
sources: Simon et al., 2023; Meza et al., 2022
practical_application: Regular heavy drinking (3-4+ drinks/day) undermines all fitness goals.

fact: Alcohol impairs muscle mitochondrial function, reducing ATP production and training performance.
sources: Simon et al., 2023; Dominguez et al., 2024
practical_application: Avoid alcohol 24h before heavy training sessions.

fact: Post-exercise alcohol (1.0g ethanol/kg, ~5-6 drinks) significantly delays strength recovery. Even 0.5g/kg may impair recovery.
practical_application: Keep to 1-2 drinks max if socializing post-workout.

fact: Abstinence improves muscle mass/function, but muscles are NOT fully restored to normal — some damage irreversible.
practical_application: The sooner you cut back, the better.

fact: Alcohol's effect on MPS is dose-dependent: 1-2 drinks minimal impact, ≥0.5g/kg causes significant MPS suppression (24-37% reduction).
sources: Bourgeois et al., 2022; Simon et al., 2023
practical_application: 1-2 occasional drinks with protein is fine. Binge drinking is the problem.

fact: Soya chunks: highest protein-per-rupee in India. ~52g protein/100g dry. Cost: ~₹0.15-0.20/g protein.
practical_application: 50-100g soya chunks daily as protein base. 100g dry = 52g protein for ~₹10-15.

fact: Whey protein concentrate: ₹1.5-2.5/g protein (Indian brands). 30g scoop = ~24g protein.
practical_application: 2 scoops/day (48g protein) costs ~₹100-120/day.

fact: Paneer: ~18g protein + ~20g fat/100g = 260+ kcal. NOT cost-effective for protein during recomp. Low-fat paneer/Greek yogurt better.
practical_application: Use paneer for flavor, not primary protein. Greek yogurt (hung curd) = 10g protein/100g at 60 kcal.

fact: Eggs: ~6g protein each at ₹0.8-1.0/g protein (₹7-8/egg). 6-egg omelette = 36g protein for ~₹42-48.
practical_application: 4-6 whole eggs for breakfast with bread and vegetables.

fact: Chicken breast: ~31g protein, 3.6g fat/100g (165 kcal). Cost: ~₹1.5-2.0/g protein at ₹250-300/kg.
practical_application: 250g chicken breast = 77g protein for 412 kcal. Ideal dinner on training days.

fact: Indian breakfast foods (poha, upma, idli) are traditionally low protein (5-8g/serving). Modifications can reach 25-35g.
practical_application: High-protein poha: add 50g soya chunks + whey. High-protein cheela: 100g besan + 2 eggs.

fact: Vegetarian Indian diet can achieve 180g+ protein/day under 2,200 kcal using whey, soya chunks, Greek yogurt, and strategic food choices.
practical_application: Cost: ~₹200-250/day fully vegetarian.

fact: Lentils/legumes: poor protein-per-calorie. 200g cooked dal = only 14-18g protein for 230+ kcal. Not primary protein sources during recomp.
practical_application: Eat dal for fiber/micronutrients, not as main protein source.

fact: Hierarchy for recomposition: 1) Progressive resistance training, 2) Total protein ≥1.6g/kg, 3) Slight caloric deficit, 4) Sleep 7-9h, 5) Protein distribution, 6) Nutrient timing, 7) Carb cycling, 8) Supplements.
sources: Synthesized from Roth 2022, Morton 2018, Layman 2024, Lak 2024
practical_application: Don't optimize #6-8 until #1-4 are consistent for weeks.

fact: ISSN recommends 20-40g protein per meal, 4-5x daily, spaced 3-4h, total 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day.
sources: Jäger et al., JISSN Position Stand, 2017
practical_application: Master template: 4 meals × 40g + 1 snack × 20g = 180g/day.

fact: Protein + carb together post-exercise does not enhance MPS beyond protein alone when daily totals matched.
practical_application: Don't worry about specific carb:protein ratio post-workout.

fact: Creatine monohydrate (3-5g/day) is the most evidence-backed supplement for lean mass and strength.
sources: ISSN position stands; hundreds of RCTs
practical_application: 5g daily, any time. No loading needed. ~₹300-500/month in India.

fact: Caffeine (3-6mg/kg, 30-60 min pre-workout) reliably improves resistance training performance.
practical_application: Strong black coffee 45 min before training. Skip if training late evening.

fact: Sleep deprivation (≤5.5h) reduces MPS, increases cortisol, and impairs recovery. Even one night of poor sleep can reduce performance 5-10%.
practical_application: 7-9h sleep is non-negotiable for recomp.
